message.content:
In a synchrocyclotron, the proton is accelerated twice per revolution.

The energy gained per acceleration is

\[
\Delta T_{\text{acc}} = eU_0\cos\Phi_0
\]

so the energy gained per revolution is

\[
\Delta T_{\text{rev}} = 2eU_0\cos\Phi_0
\]

Using \(U_0 = 190\,\text{kV}\), the energy gain per acceleration is \(190\,\text{keV}\) multiplied by \(\cos(\pi/4)\):

\[
\Delta T_{\text{rev}}
= 2(190\,\text{keV})\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
\]

\[
\Delta T_{\text{rev}}
= 380\,\text{keV}\times 0.7071
\approx 268.7\,\text{keV}
= 0.2687\,\text{MeV}
\]

The number of revolutions required to reach \(T_1 = 950\,\text{MeV}\) is

\[
N = \frac{950}{0.2687}
\approx 3536
\]

Answer: B
